en: When working with AI agents, there may be
certain tasks, certain tools
where you just don't want to let the AI
model
do it all on its own, where you may want to
ensure that a human has the final say.
And that's a concept called human in the
loop. Now, very important, it's only a
concept that matters if you're dealing with
a piece of software that supports it.
And for example, Claude or the ChatGPT
application and many other agents
do support it.
You may have seen permission popups in those
systems asking you whether you want to allow
the model to delete a certain file or to
open a certain file. And that's exactly what
human-in-the-loop is about. It's about
wrapping certain tool calls
in logic that does not auto-execute them,
but that instead enforces human oversight
where a human has to decide whether that
action should be allowed or not.
And it's simply up to the developers of an
AI agent, so of the agent harness in the
end,
which tools should have that
human-in-the-loop control step and which
tools shouldn't.
So if you're building your own AI agent, you
can also define that certain tools should
require human permission and other tools
must execute automatically.
